Just kidding, I feel like a lot has changed but many complain that it's still the same old shit. I think people are overly negative and while there are many valid concerns complaining about our country is kind of a national past time.

I was born in 1997 so a few years after the democratic revolution of 1989 that brought down 41 years of communist rule. Before WW2 we were one of the 10 richest countries on earth and communism destroyed that and left a poor society with a severe brain drain. I think the transition wasn't handled well as we adhered to IMF shock therapy and the shift was too fast and reckless. We privatized too much and sold so much of our industry, land and resources for pennies. The transition was hard for some people and many lost their jobs. The 90's were a period of wild west frontier capitalism. Boom/bust, scamming, fraud, corruption. Then we had a big banking crisis in 97/98. We then stagnated for a few years, then had some growth and then the 2008 crisis hit. Our banks were actually ok since we put some pretty well functioning rules due to the last crisis but since we are a export heavy economy (cars mostly) we were hit by the slowdown in the west. Since the crisis we have picked up pace and our macroeconomic indicators are pretty great now. Lowest unemployment in the EU, last year we had the highest growth rate in the EU that exceeded expectations and quality of life is improving. Generally we rank very well in terms of safety and personal freedom. Crime has been going down since the 90's. We are at number 6 in the global peace index and we were rated the 4th best country for expats to live in in one survey. Generally there is a big divide between the capital Prague and the rest of the country. Prague is completely first world and western. If you walk through Pařížská street it's like you were really in Paris (without all the Africans though). Prague is really wealthy and it has become one of the best cities in the world to live in in my personal completely biased opinion. Some parts of the country are still very post communist Eastern European. Some other cities are decent like Brno and Plzen. We are still a homogeneous country but the prosperity has been pulling in immigrants, mainly from Eastern Europe.

I feel we are moving in the right direction and I am optimistic about the future. I believe we have one of the most freedom loving cultures and are by some accounts the most tolerant country in the world. Not really the whole SWEDEN YES sort of tolerance, we are very anti-Muslim for example but the sort of do whatever you want man kind of tolerance. Due to this we were named the most decadent country by a study. Highest beer consumption in the world, >50% of students have smoked weed, gambling, meth, prostitutes etc. We also have some of the most relaxed gun rights in Europe. I consider freedom to be a great thing and I think in the future we will attract free thinking talent worried by the stifling conformity of some western countries. If the economic growth and other macroeconomic indicators stay this way we should be able to catch up to the west economically in a few decades. I do worry about our low birthrate (1.44 children per woman- 205/224 in the world) and the fact that we are becoming a magnet for immigrants (not that much though. The west receives much more migrants and refugees bypassed our country completely. The 90 or so Christian refugees we took in have mostly left by now). I don't really want to end up multicultural like the west. At least our immigrants are from similar cultures, mainly Slovakia, Ukraine and Russia. There aren't many Muslims here and that doesn't seem to change. In regards to politics we are cracking down on corruption, albeit slowly and we are finally passing some very important anti corruption laws. There are a few worrying trends like the attempt to censor certain websites as a way to fight gambling, and some proposed tax collection plans that would place too much of a strain on small businessmen. My favorite Pirate Party is looking pretty good in the polls so hopefully they will become big one day and fix stuff. Generally I am optimistic about the future prospects of my country.

I don't even have to name my country. It is a Western country. It has changed for the worse. In just about every aspect. Social, economic, political, judicial, etc. Nothing is as it was or should be. This can be said of nearly every Western nation.
